clue.text: Britain no longer needs a has-been PM with hit sound, "Brenda"

definitions.note: a cryptic description: the answer is what Britain no longer is

blocks.note: John Major, a former Prime Minister long out of office
the comic-book noise of a punch landing
Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda, and ER is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A jibe that Britain can do without a washed-up former premier, a punch noise and the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long nicknamed Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda'; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A country with great global military and economic influence is a major power, a status Britain has arguably lost since empire.

clue.text: The saddo possibly finished off by Archer not being big-headed

definitions.text: finished off by Archer not being big-headed

indicators.note: 'possibly' suggests one of several arrangements of the letters, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A sad case who was done for by the novelist Jeffrey Archer, minus the swollen ego.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big-headed' means capitalised: an archer with a small a is a bowman, not the peer and novelist Jeffrey Archer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone killed by an arrow or bullet from a bowman has been fatally hit by a missile, which is the plain sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Warning signals of the old swinger's habit?

blocks.note: first meaning: bright distress lights fired into the sky
second meaning: the wide-bottomed trousers of the 1970s, a habit being clothing

explanation.surface: Suggests the tell-tale signs that give away an ageing swinger's routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a behaviour pattern but is clothing, as in a nun's habit; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Flares are both distress rockets fired as alerts and bell-bottom trousers associated with seventies party-goers.

clue.text: City supporters - one has trouble getting erection

the Roman numeral for one
to ail is to suffer or be troubled

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of underwear and a man with an embarrassing difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' points at football fans of a city but means underwear; 'erection' is the upward reading in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasilia is the purpose-built capital of Brazil, designed in the 1950s and inaugurated in 1960.

clue.text: see 22dn.
Vasectomy – bargain!

blocks.note: first meaning: the slang name for the male sterilisation operation
second meaning: something cheap, a steal

explanation.walkthrough: The dash and exclamation make it sound like an advert for a cut-price operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal both for a surgical cut of the vas deferens and for a purchase at a very low price.

clue.text: Cable's dithering about his lead – or he's reluctant to take the plunge?

definitions.text: he's reluctant to take the plunge

indicators.note: dithering is wavering back and forth, so the letters are unsettled and rearranged
the lead of a word is its opening letter
about means around, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: Vince Cable, the Lib Dem politician, whose name is the fodder
the opening letter of his
taken as written

explanation.surface: Vince Cable, the Liberal Democrat, wavers over his leadership role, or perhaps over marriage.

clue.text: Old rockers swilling gin in fancy car – Blair's?

indicators.note: swilling sloshes a drink around, so its letters are churned into a new order
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a Rolls-Royce, the luxury motor
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Ageing rock stars knocking back gin in a luxury car belonging to Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolling Stones are the veteran English rock band formed in 1962, still touring with members in their eighties.

clue.text: "No Bake off for Ms Brooks" article – hearing finally put in suspense again

indicators.note: no means without, so the named letters are taken away
finally points to the closing letter of the word

blocks.note: Rebekah Brooks, the former News International chief cleared in the phone-hacking trial
a nod to The Great British Bake Off; these letters are removed
the indefinite article
the closing letter of hearing

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style quip about Rebekah Brooks's court hearing and a television baking show.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking B, A, K and E out of REBEKAH leaves REH. The surface also plays on 'suspense' as a pun on hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang something up a second time, such as a picture or door, is to suspend it once more.

clue.text: (& 22ac.) Prevent Boris from reproducing "Literary giant"?

blocks.note: with 'from reproducing': to doctor an animal is to neuter it
Boris Johnson, the politician

explanation.surface: A wish that Boris Johnson be stopped from having yet more children.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor here is the vet's euphemism for castrating or spaying a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson, compiler of the great eighteenth-century dictionary, is commonly called Doctor Johnson and was a towering man of letters.

clue.text: No more going round after this, to hold out genital area

definitions.text: No more going round after this

blocks.note: to last is to endure or hold out
the lap is the front of the lower body when seated

explanation.surface: A crude encouragement to keep going for one final round, with a smutty aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The final circuit of a race track is the one after which runners stop circling, so nothing remains to complete.

clue.text: Skip arse twerking as evening amusement

explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising and drinking at ski resorts once the slopes close for the day.

clue.text: Left before Miliband turned sour – was first to go

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
Ed Miliband, the former Labour leader
milk that has turned has gone off

explanation.surface: The political left abandoned Ed Miliband before things soured for him.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off is to open proceedings, to start ahead of everyone else in an order.

clue.text: French view over leak chain, which is hardly encouraged by Putin

definitions.text: which is hardly encouraged by Putin

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means turned upward, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
to view is to see
slang for a urination
ch. is the abbreviation for the chain, an old unit of length

explanation.surface: Evokes the rumoured kompromat video and leaks chain that Putin would rather suppress.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty to voice opinions without censorship is something an authoritarian Russian leader is known to curtail.

clue.text: After the match, an attacking move on a player's genitals

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in the answer

blocks.note: a match is a marriage

blocks.clueFragment: an attacking move on a player
blocks.note: a football or rugby challenge for the ball

explanation.surface: A sports report: after the game, a player is fouled in the groin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a fixture, which makes 'tackle' feel like part of the scene, but the match is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedding tackle is jocular British slang for the male private parts, the equipment used on the honeymoon.

clue.text: Tricky Dicky, American politician losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter is cut off

blocks.note: dicky is British slang for unwell, as in a dicky heart
the standard abbreviation
a British Conservative

explanation.surface: Tricky Dicky was Richard Nixon's nickname; an American politician brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky Dicky' reads as one name for Nixon, but 'Tricky' is the definition and 'Dicky' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deceptive and not real, like a trick of the light, is illusory.

clue.text: Kim Il let out to relieve the boredom

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: North Korea's dictator is let out of his compound to stave off tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass idle hours with some diversion while waiting is the idiom for occupying empty time.

clue.text: Blunt, very hollow, protected by party backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word reads right to left
something protected is surrounded by its guard, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: short for Labour
a rut is a groove or furrow in the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Very hollow' looks like a single phrase, but 'very' belongs with 'Blunt' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutal honesty is extreme frankness, so the word means exceedingly direct and harsh in speech.

clue.text: Tory-originated bollocks about resistance leading to the top

about means around, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: the opening letter of Tory
both are crude slang for nonsense
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Conservative-sourced rubbish about the resistance movement reaching the very highest levels.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt is a simple short-sleeved garment for the upper body, which is what a top is.

clue.text: As Ken Dodd's tense, lick his nuts?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective: as Ken Dodd's stick is, i.e. given to tickling, fair as a cryptic hint with the question mark

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

blocks.note: the grammatical abbreviation
the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A lewd suggestion about the comedian Ken Dodd, nervous and inviting oral attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a Liverpool comic famous for his feathery 'tickling stick' and the catchphrase 'How tickled I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian's trademark prop was a feather duster for tickling, so his stick is sensitive to touch in the sense that it tickles.

the fodder, taken as written
the fodder, taken as written

clue.text: Name, say, who'll give you head offensively

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: Sounds like a lewd query about who offers oral sex, crudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give you head' suggests sex, but here it means a headbutt, which in British slang is to nut someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who butts others with the forehead nuts them, and a violent madman is also called a nutter in British slang.

clue.text: One who got their oats cold comes in increasingly pissed off

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: more sore, i.e. more annoyed
the tap abbreviation

explanation.surface: A man who had sex coldly grows ever more annoyed; a crude bedroom vignette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your oats' is British slang for having sex, and to score is to pull a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has scored has succeeded in having sex, so the person who managed it is one who scored.
